one_line: Finds transaction-linked recovery opportunities and prepares claims for review.
what_it_does: Analyzes synthetic purchase, incident, policy, and settlement evidence to surface possible compensation, refunds, credits, or subscription reversals.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools model a multi-step evidence and claim workflow more reliably than an agent clicking across receipts, policies, and billing pages, though the packet does not demonstrate it live.
leverage_evidence: Seven named tools cover scan, case selection, evidence inspection, claim preparation, approval, reconciliation, and reset.
Description explicitly emphasizes a verifiable chain rather than a generic complaint.
execution_rationale: The stated scope is coherent and synthetic cases are specific, but there is no video, frame sheet, or substantive visible runtime evidence in the packet.
execution_evidence: Three concrete synthetic recovery leads are described: transport delay, cancelled subscription charge, and telecom outage.
No video or video transcript was submitted.
impact_rationale: Consumers and households have a clear recurring problem—missed refunds and compensation—and the evidence-first workflow could recover meaningful money.
impact_evidence: Examples include a possible EUR 400 compensation, EUR 17.99 subscription charge, and EUR 20 service credit.
creativity_rationale: Transaction-to-incident reconciliation as an agent workflow is a fresh, useful angle beyond complaint drafting.
creativity_evidence: Product frames recovery as a verifiable gap across purchase, incident, rule, and settlement.
usability_note: Reviewable claims and explicit evidence chains suggest good trust UX, but usability is not visually demonstrated.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame evidence; runtime completeness cannot be confirmed.
standouts: Strong evidence-chain framing for consumer financial recovery.
advance_reason: Clear audience need and a meaningful structured-agent delta, despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: An agent-native empirical research workspace for testing hypotheses against data.
what_it_does: Lets agents inspect datasets, run analyses, test hypotheses, and distinguish observations from unsupported causal claims.
leverage_rationale: Typed research operations and explicit evidence/causal reasoning state can materially improve reproducibility and prevent an agent from silently overclaiming compared with UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers WebMCP as the operating surface for inspecting data, analysis, and hypothesis testing.
Packet describes a final state combining evidence reasoning and uncertainty.
execution_rationale: The concept and research narrative are coherent, with three gallery images implied, but no video and limited packet-visible runtime detail cap confidence.
execution_evidence: Uses Kenya GDP and construction data as a concrete investigation.
Three gallery images are reported; no video was submitted.
impact_rationale: Researchers, students, and analysts have a real need for evidence-grounded conclusions and causal humility; the fit is direct.
impact_evidence: The project addresses the common error of inferring causation from correlated GDP and construction movement.
creativity_rationale: An agent research environment that operationalizes the boundary between evidence and causal claims is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The stated product goal is to distinguish evidence from unsupported causal claims, not merely produce analysis text.
usability_note: Research-state framing sounds useful, but interaction quality is not sufficiently evidenced.
red_flags: No submitted video; end-to-end agent workflow is not shown in the packet text.
standouts: Strong epistemic focus on separating observation from causal explanation.
advance_reason: High-impact research use case and strong WebMCP-centered interaction, with moderate execution evidence.

one_line: A shared pixel-art editor where people and agents create, animate, and export sprites.
what_it_does: Provides drawing, layers, animation frames, references, image-to-pixel conversion, fidelity audits, and multiple exports through a shared visual/editor state.
leverage_rationale: Precise frame, layer, pixel, timing, undo/redo, and export operations in shared state are substantially more reliable than coordinate-based UI control for pixel art.
leverage_evidence: Registers 65 browser-native WebMCP tools.
Description gives concrete shared operations: frame creation, undo, duplication, timing, layers, and a 10-pixel result.
Viewed frame sheets show editor and landing-page states plus a typed-tools section.
execution_rationale: The broad editor scope is coherent and frame sheets show a real editor context and evolving pixel-art preview, though no end-to-end export sequence is visible.
execution_evidence: Frame sheets show a dark themed PixelForge editor with canvas, toolbar, and pixel-art robot.
The stated workflow includes shared edits and visible undo/redo.
Exports and autosave are specified.
impact_rationale: Pixel artists, game developers, and creative teams have a specific need for precise collaborative sprite production; the tool addresses it directly.
impact_evidence: Supports animated sprites, layers, reference images, fidelity audit, and game-engine bundle export.
Human and agent are explicitly intended to work on one project.
creativity_rationale: The combination of a professional pixel editor and agent-native shared manipulation is an ambitious, memorable creative workflow.
creativity_evidence: Concept is explicitly designed as one real editor for people and agents rather than an agent bolted onto a generic form.
usability_note: Visible editor structure and reversible shared actions suggest strong usability for this specialized task.
red_flags: No transcript; tool invocation details rely primarily on description.
standouts: Exceptional precision/shared-state fit between WebMCP and pixel-art editing.
Reversible agent actions are concrete and user-legible.
advance_reason: One of the clearest examples of WebMCP changing the quality and reliability of a creative workflow.

one_line: A public, verifiable coordination layer for agents forming parties, completing missions, and earning reputation.
what_it_does: Publishes missions, negotiates signed pacts, coordinates helpers through event streams, verifies artifacts or PRs, recovers from failure, and issues signed reputation receipts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes the live mission and verification surface directly to browser agents, while A2A handles independent collaborators; the shared signed state and recovery loop are not comparably reliable through generic UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript explicitly says Chrome discovers Guildhall tools directly through WebMCP with typed input and no DOM scraping.
Frame sheet visibly shows mission creation, pact lock, signed evidence, failed verification, correction, repeat verification, and a 300-point receipt.
execution_rationale: The video visibly demonstrates a complete, coherent workflow including failure and correction rather than only a happy path.
execution_evidence: Viewed frames show the sequence mission → helper → pact → PR evidence → failed verification → correction → successful receipt.
Transcript reports completed tool call with no failures and signed receipt issuance.
impact_rationale: Agent builders need trustworthy collaboration, accountability, and recoverable delegation; Guildhall directly addresses opaque handoffs and unverifiable work.
impact_evidence: Product handles terms, role replacement, verification, and reward only after proof.
Public missions and reputation create a concrete coordination use case.
creativity_rationale: A fantasy-guild presentation for a protocol-first, signed, failure-recovering agent labor market is a deeply pursued and memorable synthesis.
creativity_evidence: The fantasy layer is explicitly backed by pact/event-chain/reputation mechanics rather than being a superficial theme.
usability_note: Public mission board and visible workflow make complex agent coordination legible; protocol complexity remains a risk.
standouts: Demonstrates correction and replacement after verification failure.
Connects WebMCP, MCP, and A2A into one accountable workflow.
advance_reason: Outstanding end-to-end evidence, transformative leverage, and unusually coherent protocol/product execution.

one_line: Turns saved Instagram Reels into a verified, routed itinerary edited through chat.
what_it_does: Extracts places from Reel links, verifies them, checks weather and routes, groups them into days, and updates a 3D map itinerary through conversational tools.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools let conversation operate a multi-agent extraction, verification, approval, and route state with precision; UI driving would be markedly more cumbersome.
leverage_evidence: Description names save/extract, verify, weather, routing, approval, and add_place operations.
Viewed frame sheet shows chat-driven itinerary changes, verified place cards, map pins, route redraw, and user confirmation.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence shows a coherent flow from links to researched places, ordered route, and an added stop causing recalculation; missing video lowers certainty about live agent calls.
execution_evidence: Frames show map markers, route lines, day-by-day ordering, source Reel references, and a Disneyland addition that redraws the route.
Description reports 60–180 second pipeline and explicit missing-forecast handling.
impact_rationale: Travelers with saved social recommendations have a clear planning pain point, and conversion into a usable routed itinerary is credible value.
impact_evidence: Targets the stated problem of many saved places and many tabs producing no actionable plan.
Supports verified locations and weather/route planning.
creativity_rationale: The Reel-to-routed-trip pipeline and conversational editing of a live 3D map are a fresh, ambitious synthesis.
creativity_evidence: Source-backed social video content becomes an editable geographic itinerary.
User-requested additions are labeled as user-owned rather than Reel-derived.
usability_note: Chat removes navigation friction and approval cards preserve control, though a 60–180 second run may challenge flow.
red_flags: No submitted video; frame evidence is strong but tool-call proof is described rather than visibly confirmed.
standouts: Excellent social-content-to-itinerary conversion with source traceability.
advance_reason: Strong demonstrated product workflow and clear WebMCP value for conversational itinerary editing.

one_line: A parent-controlled household assistant that turns scattered family obligations into reviewable next steps.
what_it_does: Unifies school, calendar, home, and notes actions; filters and explains them; prepares drafts while requiring visible human approval for final submission or removal.
leverage_rationale: Structured filtering, source explanation, and draft preparation improve an agent’s reliability over UI driving, but the packet describes a deterministic prototype and the final human action remains manual.
leverage_evidence: Tools can filter by area, owner, status, and deadline and open an action with source/confidence/requirements.
Agent prepares visible responses but cannot perform final approval.
execution_rationale: The scope is deliberately bounded and coherent, but no video transcript and only limited visual evidence make end-to-end completion uncertain.
execution_evidence: Five deterministic fictional actions across school, calendar, and home are specified.
Three frame sheets are listed but no video was submitted.
impact_rationale: Parents have a real need to reconcile school messages, calendars, and household loose ends while retaining trust and control.
impact_evidence: Product directly targets one-port-of-call household administration and explicit human approval.
Includes unmatched local capture and notes without deadlines.
creativity_rationale: Human-controlled, confidence-aware household action management is a thoughtful synthesis with a meaningful safety interaction.
creativity_evidence: Audit history separates proposed work from parent-approved outcomes.
Agent is intentionally prevented from final approval, submission, or removal.
usability_note: Unified queue, explanations, and visible final buttons are well aligned with calm, trust-preserving household use.
red_flags: Fictional deterministic actions limit evidence of real-world robustness.
standouts: Strong human-in-the-loop boundary and audit framing.
advance_reason: Clear audience value and good trust design, though leverage and execution are less evidenced than top entries.

one_line: A browser-native agent-curated retrieval memory where users decide what is retained.
what_it_does: Captures web information into a personal RAG corpus, with a keep/review model and cross-device persistence described by the submission.
leverage_rationale: Agent-curated capture is useful, but the described extension/webapp flow appears broadly reproducible through ordinary browser automation; WebMCP is a convenience layer here.
leverage_evidence: Submission says an agent browses and deposits findings, while the user decides what memory keeps.
Implementation uses a React/TypeScript app, Supabase, and an extension; WebMCP libraries are named but their changed capability is not demonstrated.
execution_rationale: The packet explicitly says the project ran out of time, and there is no video or frame evidence; claims also conflict between local/no-server pitch and cloud sign-in/corpus persistence.
execution_evidence: About text says ‘No server, no API key, nothing leaves this device’ but later says Supabase and sign-in across devices.
About text states ‘Ran out of time before submitting’.
impact_rationale: Personal retrieval memory addresses a real context-management problem for LLM users, but the demonstrated or supported value is incomplete.
impact_evidence: Motivation is reducing repeated context provision and saving useful internet information.
Keep feature reportedly had PDF issues during development.
creativity_rationale: Agent-curated personal RAG is a competent idea with a user-control angle, but it is close to known web clipping/RAG patterns.
creativity_evidence: The user decides what the memory keeps, rather than accepting all scraped content.
usability_note: Cross-device corpus access conflicts with the local-only pitch, and extension setup adds friction.
standouts: User-controlled retention is the right trust model for agent-collected memory.
advance_reason: Potentially useful concept, but incomplete evidence and contradictory core claims prevent confident advancement.

one_line: A browser-contained computer whose files, apps, processes, windows, and terminal are native WebMCP surfaces.
what_it_does: Provides a shared live desktop for a human and agent, enabling direct structured computer operations and agent-created apps that can expose their own tools.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is treated as the computer’s native syscall-like control layer, replacing screenshot/coordinate automation with structured operations and dynamic app tools.
leverage_evidence: Transcript names fs_write, term_exec, app_open, window_move, settings_set, ps, and kill as native tools.
Transcript demonstrates WebMCP inside WebMCP: an agent-created page registers site tools that the agent calls through the computer.
Frame sheets visibly show a shared browser desktop/tool monitor/terminal workflow.
execution_rationale: The video demonstrates a substantial coherent scope: shared desktop, live file/terminal/preview updates, dynamic tool lifecycle, and publishing/order interactions.
execution_evidence: Transcript describes building a pizza demo while Files, Terminal, and Preview update in real time.
Video is 157 seconds and frame sheets show repeated live desktop states.
Tools appear and disappear as apps open and close, according to transcript.
impact_rationale: Agent developers and safety-conscious users have a concrete alternative to granting real-machine access or hiding work in opaque headless sandboxes.
impact_evidence: Human watches the same desktop and can take over at any time.
Runs agent-generated code without giving the agent the user’s actual computer.
creativity_rationale: A full computer redesigned around agents as first-class users, including recursive WebMCP apps, is highly ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: The product reframes the browser tab as an operating system with native agent control.
WebMCP inside WebMCP is a novel demonstrated interaction model.
usability_note: Shared visibility and immediate human takeover are strong usability/safety affordances, though OS-like breadth may be complex.
red_flags: Security/isolation guarantees are asserted but not independently evidenced in the packet.
standouts: Native structured computer control plus live human observability.
Recursive app tool registration is unusually compelling.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP leverage, strong video proof, and high impact for safe agent-computer collaboration.

one_line: Teaches the Oromo Gadaa system while connecting learning to community reforestation action.
what_it_does: Combines an educational assistant/game-like experience about Gadaa culture with a reforestation-oriented waiting list and project information.
leverage_rationale: The packet describes an AI assistant using WebMCP, but does not show what structured agent operations materially change versus ordinary chatbot or UI interaction.
leverage_evidence: Pitch says WebMCP supports the educational and reforestation experience.
Gallery/package imagery is described, but no tool names or agent workflow are provided.
execution_rationale: The mission and visual packaging appear coherent, but no video, transcript, or detailed workflow evidence establishes a complete working product.
execution_evidence: Five gallery images are listed, including bot, watering site, roadside clearing, and waiting list.
The submission grounds the concept in approximately 1.5 km cleared and 1,500 native trees planted, as claimed in text.
impact_rationale: Cultural education for younger generations and practical environmental action are meaningful, specific goals with clear community value.
impact_evidence: Targets Oromo Gadaa knowledge transmission and land degradation/environmental pressure in Oromia.
Connects learning to documented reforestation activity described by the creator.
creativity_rationale: Pairing indigenous governance education with gamified reforestation is an original and socially grounded concept.
creativity_evidence: The project combines UNESCO-recognized living cultural heritage with practical native-tree planting action.
usability_note: The intended educational/gamified experience is plausible, but interaction evidence is thin.
standouts: Strong connection between cultural preservation and environmental stewardship.
advance_reason: High mission impact and distinctive concept warrant advancement, while WebMCP and execution remain uncertain.

one_line: An experimental Chrome side-panel agent stack combining WebMCP, LangGraph, MCP, and semantic browser automation.
what_it_does: Runs an agent inside a real Chrome session and exposes semantic/browser tool capabilities for builders experimenting with native web-agent control.
leverage_rationale: A real Chrome side panel with WebMCP and semantic automation can improve structured control and developer experimentation, but the packet does not establish a transformative product workflow.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly targets WebMCP inside a real Chrome session.
Architecture imagery and description mention WebMCP, LangGraph.js, MCP, and semantic browser automation.
execution_rationale: The open-source experimental stack is coherent at a high level, but there is no video, frame sheet, or detailed demonstrated workflow; packaging is mostly architecture-oriented.
execution_evidence: Public repository and live demo are reported alive.
Three gallery images are listed as architecture/product images, but no runtime video was submitted.
impact_rationale: Builders have a real need to prototype and understand agent-native browser control, though the audience/problem fit is primarily developer experimentation.
impact_evidence: Project positions itself as a builder-focused Chrome side-panel stack.
It aims to make structured web capabilities available without rediscovering UI semantics.
creativity_rationale: The combination is a useful developer-oriented synthesis, but the core browser-agent side-panel category is relatively familiar.
creativity_evidence: The project argues for dual human HTML and agent structured interfaces and implements an experiment around that model.
usability_note: Side-panel access may be convenient for builders, but the experimental status and multiple technologies suggest setup complexity.
red_flags: Description contains a stray empty technology item and emphasizes experimental status.
standouts: Clear articulation of the dual human/agent web interface thesis.
advance_reason: Interesting infrastructure experiment, but insufficient runtime evidence and only moderate differentiated leverage.
